opportunities.title: 3 MCP servers run an unpinned package
opportunities.detail: playwright, postgres, notes (Claude Desktop) fetch whatever version is newest each launch, so a bad or hijacked release runs with your tools' access the moment it ships. Pin at least the major version.

opportunities.title: 2 MCP servers are handed credentials
opportunities.detail: postgres, figma receive environment variables, usually API keys, stored in plain text in your Claude config. Know which servers hold which keys, and scope those keys as narrowly as the vendor allows.

opportunities.title: 1 remote MCP server
opportunities.detail: github runs on someone else's machine: what you send there leaves this computer. Worth checking the trust rating before pointing it at client work.

opportunities.title: 1 agent inherits the session model
opportunities.detail: An agent with no model runs on whatever you are using, often the most expensive one. Naming a lighter model for search and summarising agents cuts spend with no quality loss.

opportunities.title: 1 agent has not run in 30 days
opportunities.detail: An agent nobody calls still costs attention every time the list is read. Delete it, or move it into the one project that uses it.

checks.title: No MCP server is running twice

checks.detail: Every live MCP server is declared in a config this app can read.

checks.title: Permission rules are set
checks.detail: 2 allow, 0 ask, 3 deny.

checks.title: 3 deny rules in place
checks.detail: There is a floor under what an agent may do.

checks.title: 1 of 2 agents can use every tool
checks.detail: An agent without a tools line inherits every tool its parent has, shell included. List the tools each agent needs in its frontmatter.

checks.title: No deny rule limits the shell
checks.detail: Deny rules exist, but none of them names Bash, so any agent can run any command. A rule such as Bash(rm -rf:*) is the usual floor.

checks.title: 1 agent inherits whatever model runs it
checks.detail: An agent with no model line runs on the caller's model, often the most expensive one. Pin a cheaper model where the task allows it.

checks.title: Hooks are configured
checks.detail: Some rules run automatically instead of relying on the model to remember them.

checks.title: Default model pinned: claude-sonnet-5
checks.detail: Informational: a pinned default keeps sessions predictable.

checks.title: Prices agree with the vendor
checks.detail: This app's rate card matches what the vendor recorded for the same tokens.

checks.title: 80% of spend is on the largest models
checks.detail: $1270 of $1588 in 30 days went to the top tier. Searching files, reading logs and summarising do as well a tier down; giving those jobs to subagents on a lighter model is the usual way to cut this without touching the hard work.

checks.title: One session has been open 18 days
checks.detail: It cost $93 in the last 30 days. A session re-sends its growing history on every turn, so an old one pays more for each answer and gets slower to steer. Starting fresh for new work, and keeping what matters in project memory, is cheaper.

checks.title: Spend is attributable
checks.detail: Less than a quarter of spend is without a work area.

checks.title: 94% of your tokens in the last 30 days were context re-reads
checks.detail: A re-read is the conversation so far being sent again so the model can answer the next turn. It is cheaper than fresh input, but a one-hour cache write bills at twice the catalogue rate, which is why the spend here is a floor rather than an invoice.

checks.title: Subagents are a small share of spend
checks.detail: Less than 10% of the last 30 days went to subagents.

checks.title: Custom agents are in use
checks.detail: Specialist agents keep long jobs out of the main context.

checks.title: No subscriptions recorded
checks.detail: The app cannot say what the tools cost, when they renew, or whether each plan earns its price until the Subscriptions tab has your numbers.

checks.title: 2 client rules set
checks.detail: Spend rolls up to who the work was for.
